title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Guiding Opinions on Promoting Quality and Efficiency and Advancing Substantive Resolution of Conflicts and Disputes in Judicial Work
keywords_en: administrative litigation; administrative penalty; administrative compensation; effectively promoting substantive resolution of disputes
full_text_en:
Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Guiding Opinions on Promoting Quality and Efficiency Enhancement and Facilitating Substantive Resolution of Disputes in Trial Work

Fa Fa [2024] No. 16

The High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Guiding Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Promoting Quality and Efficiency Enhancement and Facilitating Substantive Resolution of Disputes in Trial Work are hereby issued for your earnest reference and implementation in light of actual work. Problems encountered during implementation shall be promptly reported to the Supreme People's Court.

December 23, 2024

Guiding Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Promoting Quality and Efficiency Enhancement and Facilitating Substantive Resolution of Disputes in Trial Work

To deeply implement Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law, adhere to a people-centered approach, resolutely prevent "procedural formalism," facilitate substantive resolution of disputes, achieve case closure and social harmony, and promote quality and efficiency enhancement in trial work, these Opinions are formulated in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and other relevant laws and judicial interpretations, and in light of the actual circumstances of trial work.

Article 1. In trial work, people's courts shall adhere to the performance of duties in accordance with the law, promptly and accurately respond to claims through the necessary trial and enforcement procedures, effectively protect the litigation rights of the parties, promote substantive and one-time resolution of disputes, and strive to enable the people to feel fairness and justice in every judicial case.

Article 2. People's courts shall firmly rely on the leadership of Party committees, uphold and develop the "Fengqiao Experience" in the new era, and actively integrate into the grand pattern of social governance based on co-construction, co-governance, and shared benefits.

Adhere to the principle of prioritizing mediation. For civil disputes and administrative compensation, compensation, and administrative disputes arising from administrative penalties such as fines and detentions imposed by administrative organs within the statutory range that are brought before a people's court, if mediation is appropriate, mechanisms such as people's mediation, administrative mediation, judicial mediation, and industry-specific or professional mediation may be used to promote and support prior mediation. If mediation fails, the case shall be tried and adjudicated in a timely manner in accordance with the law, and any occurrence of forced mediation, prolonged non-resolution through mediation, or pressure to adjudicate through mediation that violates the principle of voluntary mediation shall be strictly prohibited.

Article 3. For disputes brought before a people's court, the case filing registration system shall be followed to ensure that "every case must be filed and every lawsuit must be accepted." The case filing and litigation service departments of the people's court shall guide the parties to submit complaints and statements of defense in accordance with the standard model text requirements. If the matter sued falls within the scope of cases accepted by the people's court, but any of the following circumstances exist, the court shall patiently provide legal explanations and litigation guidance and inform the party of the needed corrections in a single notice, and shall not directly rule to not accept the case, not file the case, or dismiss the action:

(1) The litigation agent has not submitted a power of attorney and related supporting documents;
(2) When a legal person or other organization files a lawsuit, the materials lack the seal of the organization or the signature or seal of the legal representative or principal responsible person;
(3) The content of the complaint is incomplete or contains other errors;
(4) The defendant is identified but an accurate service address cannot be provided;
(5) The cause of action claimed is clearly erroneous;
(6) The litigation claims cannot be clearly expressed;
(7) The court receiving the lawsuit does not have jurisdiction;
(8) Other circumstances where legal explanations and litigation guidance should be provided.

For a counterclaim, addition of claims, or modification of claims filed by a party that comply with legal provisions, the court shall not refuse to accept them on grounds such as "file a separate lawsuit" or "resolve at the enforcement stage."

If the matter sued does not fall within the scope of cases accepted by the people's court, legal explanations and ideological guidance shall be provided in a timely manner, and the party shall be guided to choose other appropriate channels for relief, preventing the escalation and intensification of the dispute.

Article 4. The people's court shall conduct a one-time comprehensive review of whether the lawsuit meets the statutory conditions for filing. If it does not, the reasons shall be explained in the ruling.

If a higher people's court considers that a lower people's court's ruling to not accept the case, not file the case, or dismiss the action is erroneous and instructs the lower people's court to conduct trial, and the lower people's court finds that new facts or reasons have emerged necessitating a dismissal of the action, it shall report to the higher people's court for approval.

Article 5. For cases of joint litigation that meet the legal requirements, the people's court shall register and docket a single case and prohibit "artificial" splitting of cases. Cases that must be jointly tried in accordance with the law shall be jointly tried; cases that may be jointly tried in accordance with the law shall generally be jointly tried, except where the parties raise reasonable objections.

If a plaintiff simultaneously files separate lawsuits against two or more related administrative acts made by the same or different administrative organs, the people's court shall determine one by one whether the statutory conditions for filing are met; if the statutory conditions are met and joint trial is conducive to substantive resolution of the dispute, the court may jointly try cases in accordance with the law.

Article 6. If a plaintiff in an administrative lawsuit withdraws the lawsuit and then refiles, and is able to provide evidence proving the existence of one of the following circumstances, it shall be deemed to have "legitimate reasons," and the people's court shall accept the case in accordance with the law:

(1) The plaintiff applied to withdraw the lawsuit due to being deceived or coerced, which goes against the plaintiff's true intention;
(2) The plaintiff applied to withdraw the lawsuit after reaching a settlement with the administrative organ, but the settlement was not actually performed due to reasons attributable to the administrative organ;
(3) The plaintiff applied to withdraw the lawsuit because the administrative organ promised to resolve the relevant dispute or other practical difficulties, but the administrative organ failed to resolve the matter within the promised period or a reasonable period;
(4) Other circumstances with legitimate reasons.

Article 7. When a people's court, while hearing an administrative case, finds that a related civil dispute needs to be resolved first and that the civil dispute can be resolved together with the administrative case, it shall inform the parties to apply for a joint resolution of the civil dispute in accordance with the law. If the parties apply for a joint resolution of the civil dispute in accordance with the law, the people's court shall jointly hear the administrative and civil cases; if the parties expressly state that they do not apply for a joint hearing of the civil dispute and have not resolved the relevant civil dispute through civil litigation, arbitration, or other statutory channels, the people's court shall render a judgment on the administrative case in accordance with the law based on the available evidence.

If a people's court finds that a civil case it has accepted falls within the scope of an administrative case, it shall, after obtaining the consent of the plaintiff, promptly convert the case into an administrative case for trial. If it does not have jurisdiction over the administrative case, it shall render a ruling to transfer the case to the people's court with jurisdiction in accordance with the law. If the receiving people's court considers that the case is not an administrative case, it shall report the matter to their common higher people's court for a decision.

If a people's court finds that an administrative case it has accepted falls within the scope of a civil case, the preceding paragraph shall apply mutatis mutandis.

Article 8. A people's court shall not render a ruling to transfer a case that falls within its own jurisdiction. If a plaintiff adds a defendant to circumvent the rules on jurisdiction, the court receiving the lawsuit, when determining whether it has jurisdiction, shall require the plaintiff to submit evidence proving that the added defendant has an interest in the disputed matter. If there is no interest and no other statutory matters for determining jurisdiction exist, the court receiving the lawsuit shall render a ruling to transfer the case to the people's court with jurisdiction.

Article 9. At the first instance, the people's court shall accurately identify the issues in dispute, strengthen guidance to the parties on the production of evidence, clearly inform the parties of the legal consequences of failing to provide evidence within the time limit, and guide the parties to correctly, comprehensively, honestly, and timely complete the production of evidence.

If the evidence on file is insufficient and the parties cannot collect it themselves due to objective reasons, and they apply for the people's court to investigate and collect evidence, the court shall grant the application. For evidence that is necessary for hearing the case and that the parties do not collect themselves, the people's court shall proactively investigate and collect evidence ex officio.

Article 10. For third parties who meet the conditions set forth in Article 59, paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Civil Procedure Law and Article 29, paragraph 1 of the Administrative Procedure Law, if the parties apply to add them or the third party applies to participate in the proceedings, the people's court shall grant the application; if neither the parties nor the third party makes an application, but the participation of the third party is conducive to clarifying the facts and resolving the dispute in one go, the people's court shall notify the third party to participate in the proceedings.

If a third party who should have been added but was not files a third-party revocation action that meets the conditions of Article 59, paragraph 3 of the Civil Procedure Law, the action shall be accepted; if a third party who was notified to participate in the proceedings but fails to do so due to reasons attributable to the third party files a third-party revocation action, the action shall not be accepted.

Article 11. When accepting or hearing a contract dispute case, the people's court may, based on the complaint and statement of defense, provide the plaintiff with the following explanations:

(1) If the plaintiff claims rescission of the contract, the court may inform the plaintiff whether, in the event the claim cannot be upheld or the contract is invalid, the plaintiff requests continued performance of the contract or claims liability for negotiating in bad faith;
(2) If the plaintiff claims continued performance of the contract, the court may inform the plaintiff whether, in the event the contract is invalid or performance is impossible, the plaintiff claims liability for negotiating in bad faith or requests rescission of the contract;
(3) If the plaintiff claims the contract is void, the court may inform the plaintiff whether, in the event the contract is valid or performance is impossible, the plaintiff requests continued performance or rescission of the contract.

After providing explanations, if the plaintiff makes corresponding claims, the people's court shall inform the defendant that it may exercise the right of defense.

Article 12. At the second instance, the people's court shall carefully and comprehensively review the appellant's grounds of appeal. If the facts can be ascertained at the second instance, the court shall render a judgment in accordance with the law after ascertaining the facts, and generally shall not remand the case for retrial. If there are defects in the first instance proceedings that do not materially affect the parties' litigation rights and the judgment is correct, the second instance judgment may note the defects while affirming the first instance judgment.

If, beyond the scope of the appellant's appeal, the court discovers errors in the determination of facts or application of law that harm national interests, public interests, or the lawful rights and interests of others, the people's court shall correct such errors in the second instance judgment.

The people's court shall strive to protect the winning party's rights and prevent one party from harming the other party's lawful rights and interests through maliciously delaying litigation. In cases such as loan contract disputes where the parties have no dispute over the principal amount and appeal only regarding interest, or guarantee contract disputes where the parties have no dispute over the principal debt and appeal only regarding the guarantee liability, upon application by the parties, the people's court may render a partial judgment on the uncontested matters.

Article 13. The people's court shall strengthen the legal reasoning in first and second instance judgments, respond directly to the parties' arguments, and strictly implement post-judgment explanations to promote the parties' acceptance of the judgment and desistance from further litigation. If an application for retrial is filed against an effective judgment and, upon review, the people's court considers that the original judgment's findings of fact and application of law are not erroneous, the court may, in accordance with the requirement of substantive resolution of disputes, depending on the circumstances, have the court itself or the court that rendered the effective judgment persuade the parties to accept the judgment and desist from further litigation.

The people's court shall actively serve and safeguard enterprise production and operations, helping to create a market-oriented, law-based business environment. In cases such as construction contract disputes where the parties have no dispute over the fact of construction work and apply for retrial only regarding the performance of individual construction items such as fire protection works, or sales contract disputes where the parties have no dispute over the overall transaction relationship and apply for retrial only regarding the delivery of individual batches of subject matter, if suspension of enforcement of the original judgment, ruling, or mediation statement may seriously affect the production and operations of the enterprise, upon application by the parties, the people's court may not suspend enforcement of the parts of the original judgment not involved in the retrial application.

Article 14. When hearing administrative cases, the people's court shall, on the basis of adhering to the principle of legality review, strengthen the review of and response to substantive claims, and render judgments conducive to the substantive resolution of administrative disputes:

(1) When a people's court orders an administrative organ to perform a statutory duty or payment obligation, it shall, to the extent possible based on the relevant facts of the case, render a judgment with specific and clear content. If investigation or discretion by the administrative organ is truly necessary, and the court orders a new administrative act or remedial measures, the judgment shall provide guidance on the standards for the new act, the time limit for performance, and other matters.

(2) If a party requests revocation of the sued administrative act, confirmation of its illegality, or a declaration of its nullity, the people's court may explain that any possible administrative compensation dispute may be resolved together; in administrative compensation cases where the issue of compensation can be resolved together, it shall be handled together.

(3) If the people's court considers that the penalty is clearly improper, or that other administrative acts involve errors in the determination or calculation of amounts, the court shall, to the extent possible, directly render a judgment of variation after ascertaining the facts of the case.

Article 15. The people's court shall adhere to the governance of the "source of enforcement," actively promote the integrated management of case filing, trial, and enforcement in accordance with judicial rules, consider potential future enforcement issues at the case filing and trial stages, provide notices and warnings, and proactively guide the parties to apply for property preservation; when necessary, the court shall take property preservation measures ex officio. When drafting judgments, the court shall ensure that the subjects of rights and obligations and the content of payments are clear and enforceable, with particular emphasis on the immediate and voluntary performance of mediation statements. The court shall also carry out post-judgment supervision work to effectively increase the rate of voluntary compliance with effective judgments.

The people's court shall promptly and properly take measures such as property preservation, investigation and control, disposition, and distribution of case funds. If there is property available for enforcement, it shall be disposed of and distributed promptly; if there is no property available for enforcement, the procedures for concluding the enforcement process shall be applied properly; if there is malicious delay in enforcement or false filing of enforcement objections that abuse the right to object to enforcement, compulsory measures shall be taken in accordance with Articles 114 and 116 of the Civil Procedure Law.

Article 16. When a people's court rules to conclude the enforcement process in a case without property available for enforcement, the principle shall be that the "inability to enforce" exists only after all enforcement measures have been exhausted. Rushing to conclude enforcement solely to achieve a high case closure rate shall be strictly prohibited, and repeated conclusion and restoration of enforcement shall be avoided. The people's court shall not rule to conclude the enforcement process unless the following work has been carried out:

(1) Issuing an enforcement notice and a consumption restriction order to the enforcement debtor, and including qualified enforcement debtors in the list of dishonest persons subject to enforcement;
(2) Exhausting all means to comprehensively investigate the property of the enforcement debtor, conducting necessary on-site investigations and search measures, and legally taking necessary investigation measures to locate enforcement debtors whose whereabouts are unknown;
(3) Disposing of the property of the enforcement debtor that has been discovered, unless it cannot be disposed of;
(4) Legally taking compulsory measures such as fines or detention against the enforcement debtor or other persons obstructing enforcement, or legally initiating criminal liability procedures against enforcement debtors who have committed crimes;
(5) Interviewing and consulting with the applicant for enforcement, except for enforcement of litigation costs or property-related criminal penalties;
(6) Legally taking other enforcement measures.

Article 17. The people's court shall strengthen trial management and supervision, enhance the analysis of case quality and efficiency, promptly identify and correct problems, maximize the resolution of disputes, protect the lawful rights and interests of the people, uphold the authority and dignity of the rule of law, and maintain social stability.
